name: BMP384 pressure & temperature sensor
description: Bosch robust, gel-filled digital barometric pressure (300–1250 hPa, ±0.09 hPa relative, ±0.5 hPa absolute) and temperature (-40 to +85 °C, ±0.35 °C at 25 °C) sensor with I2C and SPI interfaces, made to resist water and liquids. The chip runs on 1.65–3.6 V. Sold as: SparkFun Pressure Sensor - BMP384 (Qwiic), SEN-19662, 7-pin header GND, 3V3, SDA, SCL, ADR, CSB, INT (no regulator or level shifting: 3.3 V only, 2.2 kΩ I2C pull-ups via the I2C jumper), I2C address 0x77 (0x76 with the ADR jumper moved to GND).
eli5: A tough, very sensitive barometer and thermometer: it feels tiny changes in air pressure, enough to tell you climbed a staircase, and its gel-filled port shrugs off splashes.

pins.name: 3V3
pins.description: Supply, 1.65–3.6 V straight to the chip (no regulator): use 3.3 V, never 5 V

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (printed SDI/SDA, SPI data in); 2.2 kΩ pull-up to 3V3 via the I2C jumper; 3.3 V logic only

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (printed SCK/SCL, SPI clock); 2.2 kΩ pull-up to 3V3 via the I2C jumper; 3.3 V logic only

pins.name: ADR
pins.description: Printed SDO/ADR: I2C address select (SPI data out). The ADR jumper ties it through 10 kΩ to 3V3 (0x77, default) or to GND (0x76); leave unconnected for I2C

pins.name: CSB
pins.description: SPI chip select (internal 100 kΩ pull-up keeps the chip in I2C mode); leave unconnected for I2C. Pulling it low once switches the chip to SPI until power-off

pins.name: INT
pins.description: Interrupt output (data ready / FIFO), 3.3 V, not needed for basic use

supplierQuery: SparkFun Pressure Sensor BMP384 Qwiic SEN-19662
buildNotes: Power 3V3 from your board's 3.3 V pin only. The SparkFun board has no regulator or level shifter: the chip's absolute maximum is 3.8 V on the supply and VDD + 0.3 V on SDA/SCL/ADR/CSB, so 5 V anywhere can destroy it.
The default I2C address is 0x77 (ADR jumper to 3V3). Cut the trace and bridge the other side of the ADR jumper for 0x76, e.g. for a second sensor.
Check the chip ID: register 0x00 reads 0x50 on a BMP384 (the same ID as the BMP388; the BMP390 reads 0x60).
Raw readings mean nothing without the factory calibration in 0x31–0x45 and the datasheet section 9 formulas; compute temperature first, because pressure needs t_lin.
Data registers are little-endian (XLSB first) 24-bit values: read 0x04–0x09 in one burst after drdy_press and drdy_temp are set in STATUS (0x03).
Leave CSB unconnected for I2C: a single low pulse on it switches the chip to SPI until the next power cycle.
With many I2C boards on one bus, open the I2C jumper on all but one to avoid too-strong pull-ups.

driver.code:
# MicroPython driver for the Bosch BMP384 pressure/temperature sensor (I2C)
# Written from Bosch datasheet BST-BMP384-DS003-11 rev 1.0:
#   register map sec. 4.2/4.3 (CHIP_ID 0x50), trimming coefficients table 23,
#   coefficient scaling sec. 9.1, temperature 9.2, pressure 9.3 (float compensation),
#   measurement time sec. 3.9.2, start-up time 2 ms (table 2).
import time

REG_CHIP_ID = 0x00   # 0x50 on BMP384
REG_ERR = 0x02       # bit0 fatal_err, bit1 cmd_err, bit2 conf_err
REG_STATUS = 0x03    # bit4 cmd_rdy, bit5 drdy_press, bit6 drdy_temp
REG_DATA = 0x04      # 0x04..0x09: press 7_0/15_8/23_16, temp 7_0/15_8/23_16 (24-bit unsigned, LSB first)
REG_PWR_CTRL = 0x1B  # bit0 press_en, bit1 temp_en, bits5:4 mode (00 sleep, 01/10 forced, 11 normal)
REG_OSR = 0x1C       # bits2:0 osr_p, bits5:3 osr_t (0=x1 ... 5=x32)
REG_ODR = 0x1D
REG_CONFIG = 0x1F    # bits3:1 IIR filter coefficient
REG_CALIB = 0x31     # 0x31..0x45: NVM_PAR_T1 .. NVM_PAR_P11 (21 bytes)
REG_CMD = 0x7E       # 0xB6 = softreset

CHIP_ID = 0x50


def _u16(b, i):
    return b[i] | (b[i + 1] << 8)


def _s16(b, i):
    v = _u16(b, i)
    return v - 65536 if v > 32767 else v


def _s8(b, i):
    v = b[i]
    return v - 256 if v > 127 else v


class BMP384:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x77, osr_p=3, osr_t=0):
        """addr 0x77 (SparkFun default, ADR jumper to VDD) or 0x76 (ADR jumper to GND).
        osr codes: 0=x1, 1=x2, 2=x4, 3=x8, 4=x16, 5=x32 (table 41)."""
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        time.sleep_ms(2)  # start-up time 2 ms
        cid = self._r(REG_CHIP_ID, 1)[0]
        if cid != CHIP_ID:
            raise OSError("BMP384 not found at 0x%02X (chip id 0x%02X, expected 0x50)" % (addr, cid))
        self._soft_reset()
        self._load_calib()
        self.osr_p = osr_p & 0x07
        self.osr_t = osr_t & 0x07
        self._w(REG_PWR_CTRL, 0x00)  # sleep while configuring
        self._w(REG_CONFIG, 0x00)    # IIR filter off
        self._w(REG_OSR, (self.osr_t << 3) | self.osr_p)
        self._w(REG_ODR, 0x00)
        self.t_lin = 0.0

    def _r(self, reg, n):
        return self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg, n)

    def _w(self, reg, val):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg, bytes([val & 0xFF]))

    def _wait_cmd_rdy(self):
        for _ in range(20):
            if self._r(REG_STATUS, 1)[0] & 0x10:
                return
            time.sleep_ms(1)

    def _soft_reset(self):
        # CMD 0xB6 = softreset (sec. 4.3.22); accepted when cmd_rdy is set.
        self._wait_cmd_rdy()
        self._w(REG_CMD, 0xB6)
        time.sleep_ms(3)
        self._wait_cmd_rdy()
        if self._r(REG_ERR, 1)[0] & 0x02:
            raise OSError("BMP384 soft reset failed (cmd_err)")

    def _load_calib(self):
        c = self._r(REG_CALIB, 21)
        # Sec. 9.1: convert the NVM integers to floating-point coefficients.
        self.par_t1 = _u16(c, 0) / 2.0 ** -8
        self.par_t2 = _u16(c, 2) / 2.0 ** 30
        self.par_t3 = _s8(c, 4) / 2.0 ** 48
        self.par_p1 = (_s16(c, 5) - 2 ** 14) / 2.0 ** 20
        self.par_p2 = (_s16(c, 7) - 2 ** 14) / 2.0 ** 29
        self.par_p3 = _s8(c, 9) / 2.0 ** 32
        self.par_p4 = _s8(c, 10) / 2.0 ** 37
        self.par_p5 = _u16(c, 11) / 2.0 ** -3
        self.par_p6 = _u16(c, 13) / 2.0 ** 6
        self.par_p7 = _s8(c, 15) / 2.0 ** 8
        self.par_p8 = _s8(c, 16) / 2.0 ** 15
        self.par_p9 = _s16(c, 17) / 2.0 ** 48
        self.par_p10 = _s8(c, 19) / 2.0 ** 48
        self.par_p11 = _s8(c, 20) / 2.0 ** 65

    def _measure(self):
        # Forced mode, pressure and temperature enabled; the chip returns to sleep afterwards.
        self._w(REG_PWR_CTRL, 0x13)
        # Sec. 3.9.2: T_conv = 234 + (392 + 2^osr_p * 2000) + (313 + 2^osr_t * 2000) us
        t_us = 234 + 392 + (1 << self.osr_p) * 2000 + 313 + (1 << self.osr_t) * 2000
        time.sleep_ms(t_us // 1000 + 2)
        for _ in range(100):
            if (self._r(REG_STATUS, 1)[0] & 0x60) == 0x60:  # drdy_temp and drdy_press
                break
            time.sleep_ms(2)
        else:
            raise OSError("BMP384 measurement timed out")
        if self._r(REG_ERR, 1)[0] & 0x04:
            raise OSError("BMP384 configuration error (conf_err)")
        d = self._r(REG_DATA, 6)  # one burst read press_xlsb..temp_msb (sec. 3.10)
        adc_p = d[0] | (d[1] << 8) | (d[2] << 16)
        adc_t = d[3] | (d[4] << 8) | (d[5] << 16)
        return adc_t, adc_p

    def _comp_t(self, uncomp_temp):
        # Sec. 9.2; returns degC and keeps t_lin for the pressure formula.
        pd1 = uncomp_temp - self.par_t1
        pd2 = pd1 * self.par_t2
        self.t_lin = pd2 + (pd1 * pd1) * self.par_t3
        return self.t_lin

    def _comp_p(self, uncomp_press):
        # Sec. 9.3; returns Pa.
        t = self.t_lin
        out1 = self.par_p5 + self.par_p6 * t + self.par_p7 * (t * t) + self.par_p8 * (t * t * t)
        out2 = uncomp_press * (self.par_p1 + self.par_p2 * t + self.par_p3 * (t * t) + self.par_p4 * (t * t * t))
        up = float(uncomp_press)
        pd4 = up * up * (self.par_p9 + self.par_p10 * t) + (up * up * up) * self.par_p11
        return out1 + out2 + pd4

    def read(self):
        """Returns (temperature degC, pressure hPa)."""
        adc_t, adc_p = self._measure()
        t = self._comp_t(adc_t)  # must run first: sets t_lin
        p = self._comp_p(adc_p) / 100.0
        return t, p

    def temperature(self):
        return self.read()[0]

    def pressure(self):
        return self.read()[1]

    def altitude(self, sea_level_hpa=1013.25):
        """Approximate altitude in metres from the international barometric formula."""
        p = self.read()[1]
        return 44330.0 * (1.0 - (p / sea_level_hpa) ** (1 / 5.255))

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from bmp384 import BMP384

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = BMP384(i2c, addr=0x77)
while True:
    t, p = sensor.read()
    print('T=%.2fC P=%.2fhPa' % (t, p))
    time.sleep(1)
